newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican gov't details first petrochem plant sales.
newsitem.headline: Mexican gov't details first petrochem plant sales.

text.p: Mexico has set aside four of its newly created petrochemical divisions to be the first opened to minority private ownership, an Energy Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters Wednesday.
The plants are: Cosoleacaque in Veracruz state, Escolin in the Poza Rica plant in Veracruz, Tula in Hidalgo state and Camargo in Chihuahua state.
About two weeks ago the Mexican government announced it had approved the creation of 10 petrochemical divisions, a step toward the long-delayed minority privatization.

The spokeswoman said the ministry will announce later this month further plans and its schedule for selling 49 percent stakes in the new companies, divisions of state-owned oil and gas company Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
Many foreign and domestic companies have said they are hesitant to enter into joint ventures with Pemex and await for further details on the sale to decide on participating.

Cosoleacaque was Mexico's top petrochemical producing plant in 1994 with output of 4.9 million tonnes for the year of a total 19.18 million tonnes. Escolin produced 280,000 tonnes, Tula produced 59,000 tonnes and Camargo produced 346,000 tonnes for the year.
